root_cause: The drawer opens via show()/showModal() but focus remains on the trigger button (or body) instead of moving into the dialog. The native <dialog> element does not automatically focus its first focusable child when shown via showModal() in this environment. The previous synchronous focus attempt in _showElement may execute before the dialog is fully ready to receive focus.
repair_strategy: Modify DialogBase._showElement to defer focus management to a microtask after the dialog is shown, ensuring the dialog and its children are fully rendered and focusable before attempting to move focus. This preserves the existing show/showModal logic while adding robust focus initialization for keyboard users.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the Filters drawer opens, focus will reliably move to the close button (#filters-close) after a microtask, allowing keyboard users to immediately Tab to the In stock checkbox, toggle it with Space, Tab to Show results, and press Enter to apply filters — all without a mouse.
functional_risks: Microtask focus may race with other microtasks in consumer code, but focus() is idempotent and safe.
If the dialog contains no focusable elements, focus falls back to the dialog element itself (which may need tabindex=-1 to be focusable).
Non-modal dialogs (show()) will also receive focus management, which may alter existing behavior for non-modal dialogs that intentionally do not move focus.
verification_requirements: After activating the Filters button with Enter, focus should be on the close button (#filters-close).
Pressing Tab should move focus to the In stock checkbox (#in-stock).
Pressing Space should toggle the checkbox.
Pressing Tab twice should move focus to the Show results button (#apply).
Pressing Enter on Show results should update the applied filter text and close the drawer.
Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to the Filters button.
